productionImplemented: Actual state.read/commit callback recognizes original variables/book and variables/chapter + big-variable keys only under an explicit App BookStore/source UUID/book URL grant.

Book identity registration borrows an immutable record array in O(1) on MainActor, locates off main and validates its revision. At most 256 already-granted offsets are retained; ordinary progress mutations do no whole-library map/index rebuild. Structural moves conservatively revoke the old lookup.

Production BookChapterStore reuses BookStore.persistQueue, owns bounded authoritative LRU/dirty state there, and retains its existing bounded read view. Normal edits publish without waiting for I/O and coalesce at most one pending list per book.

Chapter CAS checks real UUID/index/URL/revision and commits the same original chapter file before acknowledging success. A concurrent App edit is a later queued owner operation and cannot be overwritten by old CAS publication. Failed I/O leaves owner memory and the old file unchanged.

New owner cache misses use a throwing original chapter reader. Only a genuine missing file is empty; corrupt/unreadable data reaches typed STATE_IO instead of an empty owner. Legacy UI read behavior remains its historical logged wrapper.

Original short-variable JSON and >=10000 UTF-16 large-variable companion values are projected into the single existing OnlineChapterRef.runtimeVariables map and committed together in one chapter transaction.

ChapterFetchManager issues/revokes a proof of its actual existing generation token; explicit chapter grants require that same App book/chapter identity. Host cancellation/revocation/deadline tickets are checked on the queued writer and just before atomic replacement.

New fixture definitions exercise the actual state callback -> existing App chapter file -> reopened BookStore restore, plus real permission/corruption failures, stale TOC, identities and concurrent mutation. None has executed on a Swift SDK yet.
remaining: The 30 selected Swift SDK methods must actually compile and pass before this stage is accepted. Windows grammar is not Swift compilation or native execution.
Full App book-variable durable writes still require the existing shelf/reading metadata owner transaction; they are typed unsupported rather than acknowledging swallowed/debounced save errors.
Preview OnlineBook ownership has been traced but is not yet bridged. No UUID is inferred from a search result or book URL.
Full Cookie path/secure/expiry/hostOnly state shared with the existing App owner remains unsupported; no opaque second Cookie jar or header flattening was added.
Transactions across book/chapter, source/login/Cookie or other independent owners are rejected before mutation.
The traditional App route is not selected. Body needSave=false must still return through the existing OnlineReadingPipeline/ChapterCacheRepository generation fence; no JVM App body store was added.
SDK tests have not proved the actual ChapterFetchManager grant lifecycle or the full ordinary JAR -> JNI -> App product chain; these remain required.
General existing BookStore initialization/legacy UI sync I/O is outside this narrow new owner integration; no claim of whole-App performance completion is made.
reviewCorrections: Root review identified the initial write-then-conditional-view-publication CAS race. It was replaced before wiring by queue-owned durable state plus later queued ordinary edits; no false successful CAS implementation is accepted.

Root review identified new full-library index work on every main progress setter and catch-to-nil owner reads. Both were replaced by the bounded grant index/off-main registration and throwing owner reader before this prepared freeze.
All four grammar screens preserved their raw records/snapshots. They checked syntax only and were not counted as executed Swift methods.
newDerivedIndex: At most 256 explicitly granted book identities with known offsets, updated at the one existing record write point; initial search runs off main. This is not a second persistent store and normal progress does no whole-library index rebuild.
